reasoning:
The extract shows that the 5G testbeds and trials programme is meant to generate learning, but it gives no measurable success criteria. The nearest thing to success measures is the line "monitor the results of trials to build an evidence base to support the case for further investment in 5G services". This names a purpose for the trials, not outcomes to be measured. The extract carries no references or links.

There are some evaluation plans. The programme "will seek to evaluate different local models for facilitating the deployment of 5G infrastructure in different types of area such as urban and rural, and both single and two-tier Local Authorities". It will "improve our understanding of the different regulatory regimes... and report back by the end of 2018". Further, "We will report on progress by the end of 2017" and "The Secretary of State will update the Economy and Industrial Strategy Cabinet Committee". The strategy will be refreshed "on a regular basis". Together these give an evaluation focus, some timing, and a destination for findings, which is more than level 1.

The strongest counter-example to level 2 is that the success measures are thin. No outcomes, indicators or methods are named, and the "regular" reviews have no timetable. Publication is also unclear: the 2018 report has no stated audience, and the Cabinet Committee update is internal. Level 3 would need clear outcome measures, reasons for the trial design, a timetable for evaluation, and a commitment to publish the results.
